findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Run a quick reconstruction probe over a sample of both stores to confirm the achievable verified_ratio before fixing the 95% threshold, or derive the threshold from that measurement.
evidence: 'compaction has folded most pre-review EDIT events into SNAPSHOTs, so the at-review description must be reconstructed from git history'
'≥95% of v2 sidecars have their reviewed material reconstructed and verified against material_fingerprint'
Absence: no spike/measurement establishes that ≥95% of sidecars retain enough EDIT history for exact fingerprint match before the 95% number is fixed as a gate.
findings.finding: The ≥95% verified_ratio in AC2 is an asserted threshold whose achievability depends on how much pre-review EDIT history survived compaction — the plan itself states 'compaction has folded most pre-review EDIT events into SNAPSHOTs' yet commits to 95% exact-fingerprint reconstruction as a hard gate, with no preliminary measurement.
scenarios: Most tickets were snapshotted with later edits, so exact fingerprint reconstruction falls well below 95% and the AC is structurally unachievable regardless of correct implementation.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a spike step that computes the observed verified_ratio on a sample and set AC2's threshold from that measurement (or state a fallback: report the ratio without a hard floor).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that fingerprint verification tries each historical algorithm generation (matching attest._legacy_material_ok: raw/pre-330c, checkbox-only/pre-2be7, canonical/pre-reason, and current), marking a row verified when ANY generation reproduces the stored material_fingerprint.
evidence: attest._legacy_material_ok tries THREE superseded generations to match historical signed hashes: 'pre-330c (raw description), the intermediate post-330c/pre-2be7 one (checkbox-normalized, whitespace raw), and post-2be7/pre-reason-normalization (canonical description). Each used the raw no-file-impact reason.'
pass1.material_fingerprint exposes normalize_checkboxes / normalize_whitespace / normalize_reason precisely to 'reproduce an intermediate algorithm generation'
The corpus spans ~5000 REVIEW_RESULT files recovered from history — necessarily crossing 330c/2be7/reason-normalization boundaries
AC2 requires >=95% of v2 sidecars verified; a single-generation recompute mismatches every pre-current-generation sidecar and can push verified_ratio below the bar
findings.finding: The reconstruction recomputes the material fingerprint under a SINGLE (current) algorithm generation, but the fingerprint has multiple historical generations and older sidecars were signed under them, so those rows will spuriously fail verification.
findings.location: Approach step 2 ('recompute the fingerprint with material_diff.material_basis / pass1.material_fingerprint and mark each row verified only when it matches the stored material_fingerprint')
scenarios: A sidecar written before bug 2be7's whitespace normalization: its stored material_fingerprint was computed on raw whitespace; the current recompute normalizes whitespace, so the hashes differ and the row is marked unverified though the material is byte-identical.
A pre-330c sidecar over unedited material: only the raw (normalize_checkboxes=False) recompute matches.
findings.suggested_fix: In step 2, recompute via pass1.material_fingerprint across the same generation ladder attest._legacy_material_ok uses (varying normalize_checkboxes / normalize_whitespace / normalize_reason) and treat a match under any generation as verified; optionally use the sidecar's verified_at_sha to narrow which generation to expect.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconstruct ALL material_basis keys — ticket_id, description, file_impact, children, and the conditional file_impact_scope (no_file_impact_reason) — so the recomputed composite can match sidecars written over no-file-impact declarations.
evidence: material_diff.material_basis adds a fifth basis key conditionally: 'if ctx.state.get("file_impact_scope") == "none": ... basis["file_impact_scope"] = {"kind": "none", "reason": reason}'
COMPONENT_ORDER = ("ticket_id", "description", "file_impact", "children", "file_impact_scope") — file_impact_scope is a hashed basis component, not a diagnostic
The plan enumerates only description, file_impact, and child pins for reconstruction — ticket_id and file_impact_scope are not mentioned
findings.finding: The material reconstruction omits the file_impact_scope basis key, so any reviewed ticket that declared no-file-impact ('none' with a reason) will recompute a fingerprint missing a hashed component and never verify.
findings.location: Approach step 2 ('replay CREATE/EDIT ... for description and file_impact, resolve child pins from reviewed_related_material')
scenarios: A ticket reviewed after declaring 'no file impact' with a reason: its signed fingerprint hashed the file_impact_scope component; the plan's recompute omits it, so the composite differs and the row is marked unverified despite exact reconstruction.
findings.suggested_fix: Rebuild a full PlanContext (state carrying file_impact_scope / no_file_impact_reason) and call material_basis so the conditional file_impact_scope component is included exactly as the signer computed it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve how fingerprint verification handles the multiple historical normalization generations (per attest._legacy_material_ok): try each material_basis flag generation before marking a row unverified, and re-justify the >=95% verified target against that multi-generation recompute.
evidence: Plan step 2: 'recompute the fingerprint with material_diff.material_basis / pass1.material_fingerprint and mark each row verified only when it matches the stored material_fingerprint'
AC: '>=95% of v2 sidecars have their reviewed material reconstructed and verified against material_fingerprint'

Codebase fact: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py `_legacy_material_ok` tries THREE recomputation generations (normalize_checkboxes=False/normalize_reason=False; normalize_whitespace=False; canonical) because 'manifests signed before checkbox-state normalization hashed the RAW description ... the normalized recompute can never match them'

material_diff.material_basis exposes normalize_checkboxes/normalize_whitespace/normalize_reason flags precisely to reproduce these superseded generations — a single default-flag recompute will mismatch older sidecars
findings.finding: The plan asserts it can recompute and `verified`-match the stored `material_fingerprint` for >=95% of v2 sidecars using a single `material_diff.material_basis` recompute, but the codebase's own `attest._legacy_material_ok` proves stored fingerprints were produced under MULTIPLE historical normalization generations (pre-330c raw description; post-330c/pre-2be7 checkbox-only; post-2be7/pre-reason-normalization), each needing a distinct recompute to match — an unverified capability assertion that the single-basis recompute will hit the >=95% target.
scenarios: An older sidecar whose fingerprint was hashed under the pre-330c raw-description algorithm is recomputed under the current canonical basis, mismatches, and is marked unverified though its material is intact
The >=95% verified_ratio target is missed not because reconstruction failed but because the recompute used the wrong normalization generation
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror attest._legacy_material_ok: for each sidecar, attempt the recompute under all superseded material_basis generations (normalize_checkboxes/normalize_whitespace/normalize_reason permutations) and mark `verified` if ANY generation matches the stored material_fingerprint; record which generation matched in the manifest.

findings.checklist_item: Confirm whether corpus.py reuses mine_outcome_corpus.py's tested 'git rev-list --objects --all' + 'git cat-file --batch' walk (the harness's documented compaction-proof method) rather than a new 'git log --diff-filter=D' walk, or state why the diff-filter approach recovers the same compacted blobs.
evidence: Plan Context: 'docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/mine_outcome_corpus.py already walks git objects this way' — cited as prior art but the Approach specifies a distinct git method.

mine_outcome_corpus.py:_enumerate_event_blobs uses 'git rev-list --objects --all' + '_batch_cat' ('git cat-file --batch'); its module docstring calls this 'the authoritative recovery' and warns that an on-disk/naive scan silently misses '140 of 631 reviewed tickets (22%)' that are compacted.

A 'git log --diff-filter=D' walk only surfaces blobs whose PATH was deleted in a tracked commit; it can miss folded/unreachable-from-HEAD event blobs the rev-list --objects --all walk recovers, so the two methods are not equivalent for the compacted-ticket case AC-2 depends on.
findings.finding: The plan proposes new history-deleted-blob enumeration in corpus.py using 'git log --diff-filter=D --name-only' + 'git show <commit>^:<path>', a different and weaker incantation than the tested, compaction-proof 'git rev-list --objects --all' + 'git cat-file --batch' walk already implemented in the cited mine_outcome_corpus.py, without stating whether it reuses that walker.
findings.location: Approach step 1 ('reading tree files plus deleted *-REVIEW_RESULT.json blobs from history (git log --diff-filter=D --name-only then git show <commit>^:<path>)')
scenarios: Fully-compacted tickets (like the harness's dc58-af7b example) whose REVIEW_RESULT or EDIT events were folded may not be recovered by the diff-filter walk, undercounting the history-recovered set and failing AC-1's 'plus the history-recovered count' expectation.
Two divergent git-walk implementations drift over time, so a bug fixed in one recovery path silently persists in the other.
findings.suggested_fix: Factor the existing _enumerate_event_blobs/_batch_cat walk (rev-list --objects --all + cat-file --batch) into a shared helper corpus.py imports, or justify in the plan why the diff-filter=D approach recovers the folded/unreachable blobs the harness documents as only reachable via the object walk.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify the directory-scoped `git log --diff-filter=D --name-only` recovery against the known pathspec-scope drop (fsck_restore.py bug 85fa), or adopt the `git rev-list --objects --all` + `git cat-file --batch` walk the cited mine_outcome_corpus.py precedent actually uses so no recoverable deleted sidecar is silently missed.
evidence: Approach step 1: 'reading tree files plus deleted *-REVIEW_RESULT.json blobs from history (git log --diff-filter=D --name-only then git show <commit>^:<path>)'

src/rebar/_commands/fsck_restore.py:60-89 `_deleted_path_for_uuid`: 'git path simplification can drop a deletion there that a PATH-scoped walk reports. Live-store measurement on f130's lost EDIT: -- <tid>/ found 0, -- <tid>/*<uuid>* found 1; neither --all nor --full-history helped, so it is a pathspec-scope effect' (bug 85fa)

The Context cites mine_outcome_corpus.py as the precedent 'already walks git objects this way', but that harness uses `git rev-list --objects --all` + `git cat-file --batch` (lines 103, 131-135), NOT `git log --diff-filter=D`
Contradicts AC 'sidecar count is >= the tree count plus the history-recovered count' and AC '>=95% of v2 sidecars ... verified' if recoverable deletions are silently missed
findings.finding: The plan names `git log --diff-filter=D --name-only` (directory-scoped) for recovering deleted REVIEW_RESULT sidecars, but the repo's own use of this exact command (fsck_restore.py, bug 85fa) documents that a directory-scoped `--diff-filter=D` pathspec silently DROPS deletions git's path-simplification collapses (measured: `-- <tid>/` found 0, `-- <tid>/*<uuid>*` found 1; `--all`/`--full-history` did not help). The cited mine_outcome_corpus.py precedent avoids this by using `git rev-list --objects --all` + `git cat-file --batch` instead. The named command thus has a known capability gap against the plan's own completeness/verification ACs.
findings.location: Approach step 1 ('git log --diff-filter=D --name-only then git show <commit>^:<path>')
scenarios: A REVIEW_RESULT blob whose deletion commit git path-simplifies at the directory pathspec is never enumerated, so its sidecar and any material it uniquely reconstructs are silently absent from the manifest — under-counting history-recovered sidecars and depressing verified_ratio without any error.
findings.suggested_fix: Enumerate deleted blobs via `git rev-list --objects --all` + `git cat-file --batch` (matching mine_outcome_corpus.py), or add a per-uuid `-- <tid>/*<uuid>*` fallback as in fsck_restore._deleted_path_for_uuid; assert recovered count against a completeness floor so a lossy walk halts rather than emitting a silently-truncated manifest.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the canonical ordering/serialization rule (e.g. sort rows by (store, ticket_id, sidecar_timestamp), sort histogram keys, stable JSON serialization) that makes the manifest content hash deterministic across git-history reconstruction.
evidence: 'Assume rebuild-from-manifest is deterministic; the JSONL itself is not committed.'
'Rebuilding from the same store refs yields an identical manifest content hash'
Absence: no stated canonical ordering rule for enumerating sidecars, replaying EDIT/SNAPSHOT events, or serializing JSONL rows / histogram keys.
findings.finding: The plan asserts 'Assume rebuild-from-manifest is deterministic' but git-history reconstruction ordering (git log ordering, commit selection, tie-breaking between multiple EDIT/SNAPSHOT events at the same timestamp) is a potential nondeterminism source that the assertion glosses over; the content-hash key and AC3 depend on it.
scenarios: Two sidecars share a timestamp, or git returns commits in a different order, producing a different row ordering and thus a different content hash on rebuild — AC3 fails intermittently.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify a total ordering for enumeration and event replay plus canonical (sorted-key) JSON serialization, so the content hash is a function of content alone.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how git-subprocess and blob-parse failures are handled (surfaced/counted as errors, not silently dropped) so a partial recovery is observable rather than a green under-count.
evidence: "reading tree files plus deleted `*-REVIEW_RESULT.json` blobs from history (`git log --diff-filter=D --name-only` then `git show <commit>^:<path>`)"
AC: "needs no network beyond a local git fetch" — git is a hard external dependency of the build
findings.finding: The builder shells out to git (`git log --diff-filter=D --name-only`, `git show <commit>^:<path>`) to recover deleted sidecar blobs and replay history, but the plan does not state how git-subprocess failures are handled: a missing ref, a commit/blob that `git show` cannot resolve, malformed JSON in a recovered blob, or git not being present. Without this it is unclear whether such errors are surfaced (failing the build loudly) or silently swallowed (dropping sidecars and quietly under-counting the corpus).
scenarios: A commit referenced by history-recovery has been GC'd or is unreachable; `git show` exits non-zero and the sidecar is silently dropped, so the manifest's history-recovered count is lower than reality yet the build still exits 0 and appears successful.
A recovered blob is truncated/malformed JSON; if the parse error is swallowed the row vanishes with no signal, undermining the ≥(tree+history) count acceptance check.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the cache lifecycle — either a cleanup/retention rule for stale manifest-hash JSONL entries, or an explicit note that the cache is disposable and safe to delete.
evidence: "a compact JSONL corpus ... under a git-ignored cache dir with the manifest hash as the reproducibility key"
No cleanup/retirement path is described for prior cache entries as new manifests are produced over time
findings.finding: The plan writes a per-manifest-hash JSONL into a git-ignored cache dir but defines no RETIRE/cleanup path for that cache. Every distinct store-ref build produces a new keyed JSONL, so the cache accumulates stale entries indefinitely with no stated ownership of pruning.
findings.location: Approach step 3 / Scope (.gitignore replay cache dir)
scenarios: Repeated rebuilds over evolving store refs leave many orphaned JSONL files in the cache dir with no eviction, growing unbounded on a developer workstation.
